title: Prove a unitary centre0 chart and sharp fixed-output conditioning (no κ)
body:
For the actual 112-dimensional centre0 pair G/G^T, construct a unitary common complex chart S and a unitary **freely chosen output C** for every N>=112. If the output must instead equal S B S^-1, prove the sharp bound cond₂(S)>=r and the exact output norms lambda and condition lambda², where lambda=937+12√6097 and r=√lambda. The new chart changes the output convention and permits additional positive algebraic radicals; it does not retain the predecessor's smaller field or remove the native endpoint norm r.

Scope: written source-bound construction plus exact bounded corroboration. [Proof](https://github.com/ToikY/integer-mult-bounds/blob/4efad08de13caf6ddbf45720721509278d304190/research/centre0-unitary-product-chart/PROOF.md), [evidence](https://github.com/ToikY/integer-mult-bounds/blob/4efad08de13caf6ddbf45720721509278d304190/research/centre0-unitary-product-chart/VALIDATION.md), [advance claim/handoff](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19380869). Public head 4efad08de13caf6ddbf45720721509278d304190; tree475c504d4adaacb71418e007b64b7e7efd807e01, byte-identical to locally verified commit d2dd53e196c3a197104fde796040925dddf3aee4.

Validation:
- Both warning-strict normal/optimized implementations pass. Independent blind-first source-G and complement-projector digests agree; subsequent data-only checking validates all112 supplied basis columns, their full Gram matrix and source actions.
- Primary compares all12544 literal G entries, retains98 rational complement vectors, checks split products and six actual-source finite-field negacyclic fixtures at N128/256. Oracle checks112²/128²/256² split products and exact Fourier index/Gram identities; it does not independently reproduce the primary's six finite-field hashes.
- Registered replay, committed bytes/modes/source history, official export/input integrity and all four read-only Git-free empty-PATH cold runs pass. All14 external mutation cases reject on a disposable copy. First plans/code/output seals remain unchanged in RUN-RECORDS.json.
- Hosted CI did not certify this result. [Run41696887381](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/41696887381) cancelled its plan job during checkout under the workflow's10-minute limit (18:45:52–18:55:55Z). Python setup, helper tests, package selection and replay were skipped. The cancellation log is retained locally; no scientific hosted pass or synthetic test checkout is claimed. No rerun or dummy commit retriggered CI.

Fresh canonical main7c49fe32c55de02c2c873655c804b16e4c3fef0a, priority8/selected6030, source heads6667/5130, live Hub and open-PR overlap refreshed before publication. Search coverage and limitations are recorded. Card formal-interface-lemma (scope key636f26dec98e26b296e8) explicitly changes scope to this written algebraic boundary, not Lean or selected-assumption closure.

Credit Nick Petalas/PR6667 (head528e9129f181b79ec044fa23fddb378a646305c8) for the actual weighted-swap chart and released conditioning question; Brian/JoyboyBrian/PR5130 for the broader common-chart question and obstruction; Chris R/Clear1nsight5101 for the code; Dugongue/mdumitrean4948/4929, Cao Yifan/intqwq, Cinna Davis and retained native/analytic/precision/compiler lineage. Classical orthogonal normalization, isotopy and Fourier unitarity retain their usual credit. ToikY with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance and separate AI primary/oracle/static review; no independent human or proof-kernel acceptance.

Remaining: actual consumer/output conversion, all coefficient/access/restoration costs, a literal prefix circuit and rounded error budget, native normalizers/producer, targets, precision/stock/storage/compiler and recursive/outer admission. All five selected assumptions remain. No supplier admission, new kappa, merge or frontier change. Maintainer edits and auto-merge disabled.

Open next questions: [structured questions and blockers](https://github.com/ToikY/integer-mult-bounds/blob/4efad08de13caf6ddbf45720721509278d304190/research/centre0-unitary-product-chart/TASK.json). The smallest next step is binding one actual consumer to the changed output; this determines whether conversion is acceptable and what it costs. A consumer and complete invoice are missing. A literal unitary factorization with every rounded prefix bounded is a separate follow-up. Local environment: CPython3.12 standard library; no predecessor scientific suite, Lean, Docker or selected scientific replay run.
